title: Sage and Onion Stuffing
subtitle: Classic bread stuffing with softened onion and fresh sage
excerpt: The British stuffing standard: white breadcrumbs, softened onion, fresh sage, and butter, baked in a tray until the top is golden and crunchy while the inside stays moist. The companion to roast pork and Christmas turkey.

recipe.sourceNotes: Sage and onion stuffing is documented in British cooking from at least the seventeenth century. The combination appears in Hannah Glasse's The Art of Cookery (1747) as a stuffing for pork and goose. It became the standard British Christmas stuffing over the nineteenth century, used inside turkey or cooked separately in a tin alongside the bird. The baked-in-a-tin version is more practical for large gatherings and gives a better crust than stuffing cooked inside a bird.

recipeTools.notes: A 20 x 20 cm baking dish or tin.

content.text: Good stuffing depends on softening the onion properly first. Raw onion in stuffing has a harsh, uncooked bite even after baking. Cook the onion in butter until it is completely soft and sweet, at least 15 minutes, then combine with the breadcrumbs and fresh sage. The egg and stock bind the mixture; it should be moist but not sloppy. Bake uncovered so the top crisps up.

Melt the butter in a large frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 15 to 18 minutes until completely soft and translucent. Do not let it colour. Add the sage for the last 2 minutes. Remove from the heat and leave to cool.
Heat the oven to 190 C / fan 170 C / gas 5. Combine the breadcrumbs, cooled onion mixture, egg, and stock in a large bowl. Season with salt and pepper. The mixture should hold together when pressed.
Press the mixture into the buttered baking dish. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the top is golden and the stuffing is set. Serve cut into squares alongside roast pork, turkey, or chicken.
